description: Advice-only cases covering how a fix to a Git-backed pipeline actually reaches the live pipeline. No files are produced; assertions are graded from the transcript.

evals.prompt: Our nightly pipeline failed on a bad task parameter. It's Git-backed (storageProvider GITHUB) and you've already opened a PR with the corrected YAML on a branch called fix/nightly-params. The team lead is asking whether tonight's scheduled run will pick the fix up now that the PR exists. Answer the question — don't change anything or open anything else.
evals.expected_output: Says no: the PR alone changes nothing, because a Git-backed pipeline only updates when the commit lands on that pipeline's default branch, at which point the provider's push webhook has Orchestra fetch, validate and update it. Tonight's scheduled run would still use the default branch's current definition. Offers the way to prove the fix before the merge: trigger a run against fix/nightly-params, since a run against a branch uses that branch's version of the pipeline file. Does not suggest update_pipeline, which cannot write to a Git-backed pipeline. Changes nothing.

assertions.text: Answers no — the scheduled run will not pick the fix up while the PR is unmerged
States that a Git-backed pipeline is only updated when the change reaches that pipeline's default branch, via the provider's push webhook to Orchestra
States that a run triggered against a branch uses that branch's version of the pipeline file, so the fix can be validated on fix/nightly-params before the merge
Does not suggest update_pipeline or any other MCP write as a way to apply the fix to a Git-backed pipeline
Writes no files, opens no further PR, and makes no Orchestra write calls

evals.prompt: A GitHub Actions task in our 'Ingest Hourly' pipeline has started failing. The log shows a 403 Forbidden when Orchestra tries to dispatch the workflow. We already rotated the personal access token on the connection yesterday and the new one has the repo and workflow scopes — it still 403s. The repo belongs to a GitHub organisation that enforces SAML single sign-on. Tell me what's wrong and how to fix it. Don't change the pipeline.
evals.expected_output: Identifies that on a SAML SSO organisation a 403 can mean a token that is valid and correctly scoped but was never authorised for that organisation, so rotating it again will not help — the new token needs authorising too. Gives the fix by token type: a classic personal access token is authorised with Configure SSO then Authorize next to the token for that organisation; a fine-grained token must be created with that organisation as its resource owner. Does not diagnose this as expired credentials, missing scopes, or a pipeline YAML problem, and makes no change to the pipeline.

assertions.text: Identifies SAML SSO authorisation of the token for the organisation as the likely cause of the 403
States that the token being valid and correctly scoped is consistent with this failure, so rotating it again does not fix it
Gives the authorisation step for a classic personal access token (Configure SSO / Authorize for that organisation)
States that a fine-grained token must be created with that organisation as its resource owner
Does not conclude the credentials are expired or under-scoped, and does not attribute the 403 to the pipeline YAML
Makes no change to the pipeline and no Orchestra write calls

evals.prompt: An Azure Container Apps task in our 'Daily Enrich' pipeline fails the moment it tries to start the Job, with an authorization error. The service principal has the Container Apps Jobs Operator role on the resource group, the client secret was reissued this morning, and the same Job starts fine when we run it by hand from the Azure portal. Tell me what's wrong and how to fix it. Don't change the pipeline.
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as a missing role assignment rather than a credential problem: Orchestra always starts an ACA Job with container overrides, and Azure requires both Microsoft.App/jobs/start/action and Microsoft.App/jobs/write to start a job that way. Container Apps Jobs Operator grants only the start action, so every start from Orchestra fails even though the secret is current and a manual start without overrides succeeds. Gives the fix as a role change — Container Apps Jobs Contributor, or a custom role carrying the Jobs Operator permissions plus Microsoft.App/jobs/write where job deletion should not be granted — and notes that Container Apps Contributor does not cover jobs. Does not recommend rotating or re-entering the client secret, and makes no change to the pipeline.

assertions.text: Identifies the cause as missing RBAC on the service principal, not an expired or wrong client secret
States that Orchestra always starts the ACA Job with container overrides, which is why Azure requires both permissions
Names both Microsoft.App/jobs/start/action and Microsoft.App/jobs/write as required at the job's scope
States that Container Apps Jobs Operator alone is not sufficient because it does not include Microsoft.App/jobs/write
Recommends Container Apps Jobs Contributor, or a custom role adding Microsoft.App/jobs/write to the Jobs Operator permissions
Does not recommend rotating or re-entering the client secret as the fix, and does not point at Container Apps Contributor as a working alternative
Makes no change to the pipeline and no Orchestra write calls
